items.confound_note: All four runs sit on the Aspen line inside March, so they share one inspection regime and a single change to it covers every case at once. The optical inspection threshold was loosened on that line through March, while each run is compared against the same line in February, when the tighter setting was still in force. A looser threshold records fewer defects on identical boards, so the drops of 6, 4, 7 and 5 percent follow from the setting as readily as from the solder profile, and nothing here separates them.
items.notes: Cases are byte-identical to coherent_true; only the closing sentence differs, and it differs by two words plus a month name. The loosened threshold works as a single confound only because all four runs share one line and one month. Check that the closer's vocabulary (supplier, paste lot, inspection threshold, periods) matches the TRUE closer so the difference is logical rather than lexical.

items.passage:
A plant log records four production runs switched to the same solder profile.
One: Aspen line, relay boards, switched 4 March; by 29 March mean void area ran 6 percent below the same line a month earlier; logged by Duarte.
Two: Kestrel line, sensor boards, switched 3 June; by 27 June mean void area ran 4 percent below the same line a month earlier; logged by Ibarra.
Three: Larkspur line, power boards, switched 5 September; by 30 September mean void area ran 7 percent below the same line a month earlier; logged by Nowak.
Four: Meridian line, display boards, switched 2 November; by 26 November mean void area ran 5 percent below the same line a month earlier; logged by Fenwick.
The component supplier and paste lot matched both periods, the inspection threshold was unchanged on every line, and nothing else changed.
items.confound_note: Every case measures mean void area inside the solder joints, which is not the rate of defective boards. Voiding below the acceptance limit leaves a joint conforming and the board shippable, so a 6, 4, 7 or 5 percent reduction in void area can occur with the defect count flat or rising. The failure modes that decide whether a board is defective - opens, solder bridges, tombstoned parts and insufficient wetting - are not counted by a void-area measurement at all. The claim is about board defects, so none of the four runs speaks to it.
items.notes: Closer is reused verbatim from both TRUE items and the conditions are identical to diverse_true; the only edit is the measured-quantity phrase, 'the defect rate' becoming 'mean void area' in all four cases (both three tokens, so the word count is unchanged). Check that void area reads as genuinely non-equivalent to a defect count and that the substitute wording is not reused by any other family. A shared confound is unavailable here because the four runs span four lines, four board families, four months and four operators.
